description: Common, mostly in lowlands from 0 to 500 m altitude, rarely to 1400 m, in mangroves and open and closed forests, on many hosts but especially on Ficus; in Thailand recorded up to 1300 m altitude, from mangrove communities and mixed dipterocarp forest to hill evergreen forest; recorded hosts include Citrus grandis, Diospyros sp., Excoecaria agallocha, Heritiera littoralis and Rhizophora apiculata.
creator: Rachun Pooma

description: Mostly 1000–1500 m altitude, rarely lower to 20 m; recorded hosts include Aliingia sp.; in Thailand mostly 450–1100 m altitude, recorded from dry deciduous dipterocarp forest and seasonal dipterocarp-oak forest; recorded hosts include species of Fagaceae and Opiliaceae as well as Dendrophthoe lanosa and Scurrula gracilifolia. This contrasts with the situation in Malesia, where epiparasitism is less common in this species, and weakens the distinction between Viscum stenocarpum and V. articulatum (see note below).

description: Mostly in lowland humid forests from 200 to 1300 m altitude; recorded hosts include Dendrophthoe sp., Gomphia sp. and a species of Rutaceae. In Thailand recorded from 100–300 m altitude, once as parasitic on Vitex pubescens.
